title: Choosing between needs: neural circuits of feeding–social behavioural prioritisation in rodents
title_zh: 啮齿类动物进食与社交行为优先级的神经电路
abstract: Animals constantly face competing physiological and social demands and must flexibly prioritise behaviour according to internal state and environmental context. This narrative review synthesises current evidence on how rodents prioritise between feeding and social interaction, focusing on the neural mechanisms through which internal and affective states, reward value, and environmental context shape behavioural prioritisation. We integrate findings from social-food preference, effort-based choice, and approach-avoidance paradigms, and review the contributions of hypothalamic, mesolimbic, amygdala, and prefrontal circuits, together with neuromodulatory systems such as dopamine, oxytocin, and acetylcholine. Across these systems, behavioural prioritisation emerges from the dynamic interaction between internal states, environmental demands, and competing motivational tendencies, rather than from a fixed hierarchy of needs, and is continuously updated by prior experience and behavioural outcomes. We conclude by considering how disruption of these mechanisms may contribute to maladaptive prioritisation in addiction, anxiety, and social dysfunction.
abstract_zh: 动物不断面临竞争的生理和社交需求，必须根据内部状态和环境语境灵活优先考虑行为。本综述综合了啮齿类动物在进食与社交互动之间优先级选择的现有证据，重点阐述了内部和情感状态、奖励价值以及环境语境如何通过神经机制影响行为优先级。我们整合了社交-食物偏好、基于努力的选择以及接近-回避范式的研究成果，并综述了下丘脑、 mesolimbic、杏仁核和前额叶电路以及多巴胺、催产素和乙酰胆碱等神经调节系统的贡献。在这些系统中，行为优先级源于内部状态、环境需求和竞争性动机倾向之间的动态相互作用，而非固定的需求层次，且会因先前经验和行为结果而持续更新。我们通过考虑这些机制的紊乱如何导致成瘾、焦虑和社交功能障碍中的病理性优先级选择来结束综述。
